subject: Handshake & routing mismatch — escape-hatch request
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2029-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Handshake & routing mismatch — customer demo hit session switch

Team — quick heads-up from the Chartwise demo this morning. Emma reported a repeatable case where a slow upstream retry causes the SDK client to reattach to a different runtime instance, which in turn loses the session affinity (KV cache) and produces a long tail of token latency / partial responses.

Summary:
- Customer: Chartwise (demo environment)
- Behavior: mid-request retry -> different backend -> KV cache miss -> latency spike + partial generation
- Repro: Happens reliably when sequence length ~2k and we trigger a transient socket timeout (they simulated by dropping packets).

Attachments: handshake-sample.txt, trace-snippet-1120.log

Asking:
1) Platform/runtime: can you confirm whether retry handshakes carry the same session_id/route_hint today?
2) Sales/CS: I need a short mitigation we can give Emma ASAP (30–60m preferred) before we start a formal triage.

Jordan
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-11-20T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Handshake & routing mismatch — customer demo hit session switch

On 2029-11-20 09:12, Jordan Blake wrote:
> Team — quick heads-up from the Chartwise demo this morning...

Thanks for the triage, Jordan. Short-term mitigation ideas:
- Ask the SDK to set a persistent header "X-Session-Id" on every attempt and ensure client retries reuse it. That should keep routing consistent.
- If possible, lower the client retry count for the demo to avoid the second attachment that loses affinity.

I'll volunteer to draft a one-paragraph mitigation we can paste to Emma. Karthik — do you see any immediate risk with forcing the session header at the SDK layer?

— Logan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-11-20T13:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Handshake & routing mismatch — escape-hatch request

Jordan / Logan — thanks for the context and the traces. I pulled the snippet (trace-snippet-1120.log) and reproduced the handshake path in our staging cluster. Observations:

- The retry code path currently issues a new session handshake when the previous socket closes unexpectedly. The new handshake does not always include the original route_hint unless the client sets and preserves a session header.
- That means the RD runtime might select a variant-pool instance that doesn't have the KV cache warm for that session.

Short-term (hours):
- We can ship a micro-SDK patch that preserves "X-Session-Id" across retries and ensures it is sent as part of the initial handshake. That should preserve affinity. I estimate a patch + hotfix can be validated in ~6h (canary first).
- As an immediate customer-facing mitigation: ask Chartwise to temporarily reduce retry count and enable client-side session header (we can share a small snippet).

Medium-term (weeks):
- Runtime change: accept a client-provided "route_hint" in handshakes and prefer variant-pool affinity when provided. I'll open SUP-3421 and add acceptance criteria.
- Add telemetry: handshake->routing decisions should log original_session_id and chosen_variant so we can quickly verify in prod.

I've attached handshake-sample.txt showing the missing headers. I'll create SUP-3421 and link once created.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Emma Porter <emma@chartwise.com>
Cc: BrightLane Ops <ops@brightlane.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-11-21T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Handshake & routing mismatch — escape-hatch request

Emma — thanks again for the demo and the test traces. Quick mitigation steps you can try now while we triage on our side: 

1) In your SDK client, set a persistent header on each request:
   - Header: X-Session-Id: <random-uuid-for-demo>
   - Ensure the same header value is reused across retries for the same logical user session

2) Temporarily reduce retry count to 1 and increase per-request timeout to 8s to avoid a second handshake attempt during transient network blips.

Patch we plan to ship from Redwood (ETA ~6 hours): a small SDK patch to preserve X-Session-Id across retries and include it in the handshake. Karthik will run a canary and give us a rollback window.

If you want, I can apply these settings for your demo environment (we have access) and run a quick replay. Do you have a 20-minute slot this morning?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Folks — flagging this as a high-priority customer experience risk for Chartwise (deal HW-8421). Approve the short-term SDK patch and canary. Operational asks:
